card: Adds a TxCollection mining IPC interface allowing external services, like Stratum v2 Job Declarator Servers, to assemble and validate candidate block templates from a list of witness transaction IDs using the node's mempool. External template validators currently maintain a duplicate mempool mirror outside Bitcoin Core and repeatedly poll full templates or missing transactions, wasting memory and IPC bandwidth. The interface checks WTXIDs against the mempool, allows callers to supply missing transactions, and validates the assembled candidate block against the active tip using TestBlockValidity with an optional caller-supplied coinbase. The change is demonstrated against the Stratum v2 reference implementation in sv2-apps pull request 599.
changed_since_previous: Added commit 8b31c307b5, which allows TxCollection::makeTemplate() to accept an optional caller-supplied coinbase transaction and validate the candidate block with it instead of only supporting a node-generated dummy coinbase.
evidence: PR description: 'The Stratum v2 spec defines a Job Declarator Server (JDS), whose job it is to approve custom miner templates. It currently maintains its own mempool mirror, which it populates by repeatedly calling getBlock() and waitNext()... The new TxCollection interface introduced by this PR removes the need for such a mirror mempool.'
Author references an end-to-end integration PR demonstrating the workflow against the Stratum v2 reference implementation: https://github.com/stratum-mining/sv2-apps/pull/599

PR description notes additional potential utility for weak-block reconstruction in decentralized mining: 'may be useful for the p2pool revival project, which needs a way to validate and relay weak blocks as compact blocks.'
problem: External mining coordinators that approve miner-selected templates (such as Stratum v2 Job Declarator Servers) must maintain a duplicate mempool mirror outside Bitcoin Core. Populating this mirror requires repeatedly polling full block templates or missing transactions, wasting memory and IPC bandwidth.

risk.why: Flaws in external template assembly or validation could lead mining infrastructure to accept invalid candidate blocks or reject valid miner-declared templates.

scope_notes: Adds node::TxCollection, updates IPC Cap'n Proto definitions for Mining, refactors BlockAssembler::CreateCoinbaseTx(), and includes dedicated unit tests and Python IPC functional tests.
summary: Adds a TxCollection interface to the mining IPC and node subsystems, enabling external callers to construct and validate block templates from an ordered list of witness transaction IDs (WTXIDs). Matches requested WTXIDs against the local mempool, identifies missing transaction positions, ingests missing raw transactions, and validates the assembled block against the chain tip using TestBlockValidity. Also extracts reusable coinbase generation from BlockAssembler into a helper, supports an optional caller-provided coinbase for validation, and disables template-mutation methods on externally assembled templates.
